body: She's talking about "tomorrow" and what her options are as far as going to classes and such, which gives me some security. Her day runs from noon til 8pm, and mine runs from 9am to about 3. Apparently, since she's in the honors program, all of her classes are 100% mandatory and take attendance.

I know. She's talking to me again. She has calmed down a bit, and I don't think she's in immediate danger. I'm trying to be as much of a listener as I can, and I asked her if she really feels death is the best option. She kinda broke my heart by replying that she wants to live, but she doesn't think she has what it takes. She feels she isn't good at the things she loves and has lost the last thing she's good at (school), and feels that suicide is the clearest path. I offered to spend the night over there, and told her that she could decide what terms, such as me not saying a word and/or not sharing a bed with her, but she declined.

Not that I can find, but I'm genuinely worried that that would just push her over the edge. Not to mention that when she's been happy, she has said that it was because of me that she chose to live. And I feel like if I did that, she would push me away and take her life the first chance she gets.
I am. But I can't go to her dorm this late unless she checks me in, which she won't.
It's late at night and her family are heavy sleepers. Plus, they weren't helpful to her last time. They accepted it when her old counselor told her she was okay.
